facts.text: A metric is any measured quantity; a key performance indicator (KPI) is a metric selected with a target value to judge whether a system or project is succeeding.
facts.quote: A metric is any quantity you measure, and a key performance indicator (KPI) is a metric that has been chosen, with a target value, to judge whether the system or the project is succeeding.

facts.text: Braking-system verdict functions should record first valid detection, time to collision at detection, intervention time, stopping margin, closest approach, false-warning duration, unnecessary braking, deceleration and jerk, sensor degradation state, and the operator-warning sequence, rather than only collision outcomes.
facts.quote: first valid detection, time to collision at detection, intervention time, stopping margin, closest approach, false-warning duration, unnecessary braking, deceleration and jerk, sensor degradation state and the operator-warning sequence [Chapter 9]

facts.text: Braking-system KPIs drawn from recorded verdict metrics include detection rate per encounter by stratum, false warnings per operating hour, unnecessary brake events per hour, intervention timing, and productivity loss.
facts.quote: From these the KPIs are drawn: detection rate per encounter by stratum, false warnings per operating hour, unnecessary brake events per hour, intervention timing and productivity loss.

facts.text: A few scenario-level performance values exist in off-road standards.
facts.quote: a few scenario-level performance values exist in off-road standards

facts.text: Fleet-statistical KPIs such as field detection rate and false alarms per operating hour appear in no off-road standard or regulation, according to the booklet's gap finding.
facts.quote: fleet-statistical KPIs such as detection rate in the field and false alarms per operating hour appear in no off-road standard or regulation

facts.text: The off-road braking-system program must define and defend its own fleet-statistical KPIs because off-road standards and regulations do not supply them.
facts.quote: so the program must define and defend its own [Chapter 3, Chapter 9]

facts.text: A "no false brakes" KPI creates the wrong incentive for a braking system because suppressing nuisance interventions can increase late or missed braking.
facts.quote: A "no false brakes" KPI creates the wrong incentive, because suppressing nuisance interventions can increase late or missed braking

facts.text: A detection-only KPI can produce a braking system that stops production.
facts.quote: a detection-only KPI can produce a system that stops production.

facts.text: The booklet recommends joint safety and productivity criteria for evaluating the braking system.
facts.quote: The booklet asks for joint safety and productivity criteria [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Euro NCAP's virtual-testing regime requires KPIs with tolerances as part of the dossier.
facts.quote: Chapter 2 notes that Euro NCAP's virtual-testing regime requires KPIs with tolerances as part of the dossier [Chapter 2].

facts.text: KPIs chosen before testing constitute the braking-system program's pre-registered claims.
facts.quote: The KPIs chosen before testing are the pre-registered claims

facts.text: Metrics recorded in every test run provide the raw material for claims the braking-system program may need later.
facts.quote: the metrics recorded in every run are the raw material for any claim the program may need later.
